title: Citi downgrades US stocks to 'neutral' as AI sell-off, regulatory risks mount - The Economic Times

US Markets Powered By As on 10 Nov 2026, 02:06 AM IST S&P 500 Top Gainers Trade Desk 15.13 (16.98%) Monolithic Power Systems 1,391 (16.85%) Advanced Micro Devices 513.92 (14.45%) Teradyne 246.93 (13.16%) Gainers » S&P 500 Top Losers Coterra Energy 32.56 (-8.62%) NVIDIA 177.46 (-4.92%) First Solar 191.80 (-4.65%) Molina Healthcare 201.32 (-3.67%) Losers » For live updates on US Markets, click here Citi also cut its ratings on the global and European technology sectors to “neutral” from “overweight.” Democrat victories in last week’s US midterm elections, including in states where opposition to new data centres has grown, raised fears that stricter regulations could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that helped propel stocks to record highs this year. Live Events The sell-off erased about $3 trillion from the market value of S&P 500 companies. “Volatility has now turned more broad-based, with a sizable sell-off across regions and sectors in recent days,” Citi told Reuters. Also Read: Fed’s Barkin urges rate policy caution, Goolsbee warns of inflation concerns as AI risks loom The brokerage upgraded European equities excluding the UK, citing their lower exposure to technology-sector volatility and greater sensitivity to falling oil prices. At the sector level, Citi raised global healthcare and European food and beverage stocks to “overweight” from “neutral.” (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies.
